solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Surface of river reflected man in garden

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Adam was the first man, placed in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: A puzzling local-news item about a river surface mirroring a man standing in his garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns CAM into MAC. 'Surface' is the definition, not part of the river picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road surface of compacted broken stone, named after John McAdam.

clue.text: Enormous characters in gym, on steroids

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, sitting inside the following words make the answer

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder made enormous in the gym by steroid use.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, monster means huge or gigantic, as in a monster truck.

clue.text: Charlie regularly decries Birmingham thinker

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: Brum is the colloquial name for Birmingham, an English city

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie keeps criticising a Birmingham intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinker' looks like a person but is the part of the brain that thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the main part of the brain, the organ that does the thinking.

clue.text: Doctor Kildare finally trapping medical equipment in zip

indicators.note: trapping means holding the other piece inside
finally picks out the final letter of the name Kildare

parts.note: an IV is an intravenous drip used in hospitals

explanation.surface: TV's Dr Kildare at last catching hospital kit inside a zipped bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Kildare is a TV doctor of the 1960s; 'zip' means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip and drive both mean energy and determination, nouns for vigour.

clue.text: Maori just breaking hearts?

indicators.note: breaking the words apart lets their letters re-form in a new order

explanation.surface: A Maori man is just breaking hearts, a romantic heartbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags hearts as one example of the class in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, hearts and spades are the higher-scoring suits; hearts is an example of one.

clue.text: Role of Charlton police after soup stolen from bordello

indicators.note: after places the police abbreviation behind what remains of the bordello
something stolen is taken away, so the soup's letters are removed from the bordello word

parts.note: a bordello is a brothel
broth is a thin soup
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A lurid crime story: police arrive after soup has been pinched from a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bordello' must first become its synonym before the soup is taken out of it; 'Charlton' is the actor Charlton Heston, not the London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton Heston played the Spanish hero Rodrigo Díaz in the 1961 film epic of that title.

clue.text: Simply sail off in case of emergency

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the outer pair
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
off means gone wrong, so the letters of sail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailing advice: simply set off in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like setting sail but marks the four letters as rearranged; 'case of' means only the outer letters of emergency are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something simply means doing it without difficulty, an adverb match.

clue.text: Capital extremely tense after cold weather

indicators.note: after places the capital and tense pieces behind the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A tense atmosphere in a capital after a cold snap.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is the prevailing weather of a region over time, a close relation.

clue.text: Lived and died on edge

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
a welt is a strip forming the edge of a shoe or garment

explanation.surface: An epitaph-like summary of someone who lived and died dangerously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous, but 'on' only joins D to WELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past of dwell, meaning resided, so it matches lived.

clue.text: Ivy signs letter whose contents form word picture

indicators.note: contents are what lie inside, so each word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Ivy signs off a letter that paints a vivid scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' reads as a person's name, but it is just one of three words whose insides are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a brief descriptive sketch in writing, painting a scene with words.

clue.text: Secret boozer with beer, half-cut

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn

indicators.note: cutting off half the word beer keeps only its back half

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off to the pub for a beer and ends up half-cut, tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut', British slang for tipsy, here means BEER loses half, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Fermenting juice isn't wrong

indicators.note: fermenting liquid is in turmoil and changing, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A winemaker's verdict that letting juice ferment is perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong is an unjust act, a noun synonym for an injustice.

clue.text: Stick around, and ultimately you'll achieve celebrity

indicators.note: turned around, the stick word is read from its end

parts.note: a baton is a stick, as passed in a relay

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Encouraging advice that persistence is the route to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' reads as stay put; it is a stick turned around. 'celebrity' is a person here, not fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction, which a celebrity is: both are nouns for famous figures.

clue.text: Tear about Long Island with a dependent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tear word goes round the rest

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip in fabric
LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island, New York

explanation.surface: Someone rips around Long Island with a child or other dependant in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as rushing, but it is a rip, RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dependent on something means relying on it, the adjective sense here.

clue.text: Reportedly rejected everywhere

indicators.note: reportedly marks words as heard rather than seen, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: rejected things are thrown away, or threw out

explanation.surface: A news-style claim that something was turned down by all and sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found in every part of a place is present all over it, an adverb match.

clue.text: Despondent Scottish football team heading away from Wick

parts.note: Hearts is Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which goes away

explanation.surface: A gloomy Hearts side trudging away from Wick, a town in northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsick means low in spirits, deeply dejected, an adjective pair.

clue.text: Drove female mad at last

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A man drove a woman crazy in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a drove of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a flock or mass of animals being moved together, the same as a group of cattle.

clue.text: Anil perhaps heard to choke on jam?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting on top, so this piece comes first
heard means the sound of the words counts, not their spelling

parts.note: to die is to choke in the sense of failing at a crucial moment
to jam is to stuff, cram full

explanation.surface: Someone chokes on a mouthful of jam, apparently audibly.
explanation.walkthrough: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil, or indigo, is one example of a colouring substance used to dye cloth.

clue.text: Means to suppress report

parts.note: reads as censoring news, but the report is a gunshot muffled by a device on the barrel

explanation.surface: A way to bury a news story or official document.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's report is its bang; the attachment on the muzzle damps that noise.

clue.text: Carve sides of elegant church

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut decorations into the walls of a fine church.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave or incise a design is to cut it into a surface, which carving also does.

clue.text: Carpet originally came with guarantee

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A rug sale where the carpet came with a warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is British for to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted means being reprimanded, so to carpet is to rebuke, as is the verb here.

clue.text: Play with mates until very late

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child pleading to play with friends till bedtime and beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated adjective for something done at the latest possible moment, i.e. extremely tardy.

clue.text: Close-fitting garment giving rise to bother in university

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: drat is a mild curse, like bother

explanation.surface: A clingy outfit causing trouble on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' turns DRAT IN U upwards into UNITARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A unitard is a one-piece skin-tight leotard covering legs and torso.

clue.text: Makes different V-sign

parts.note: V is taken as written
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A rude two-fingered gesture changes everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign, a British rude gesture, is split: V plus a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary something is to alter it, so varies means alters.

clue.text: Touching delicacy on fiddle

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a fiddle
tact is delicacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A tender remark about a delicate touch on the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delicacy' suggests a treat to eat and 'fiddle' a violin; they are TACT and a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical contact is the state of things touching each other.

clue.text: Read out tawdry tweet

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: tawdry means cheap and showy

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a tasteless social-media post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweet' suggests social media, but it is a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the shrill chirp of a young bird, a bird's tweet.

clue.text: Backsliding setter's packing trunk for drug dealer

indicators.note: packing means the trunk word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a chest is a trunk, a large box

indicators.note: sliding backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: setter's stands for the setter is, i.e. I'm

explanation.surface: A villain's tale: a relapsing setter stuffs a trunk for a narcotics trafficker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug dealer' sounds criminal but is the innocent pharmacist; IM reversed gives MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist sells medicines, so is literally one who deals in drugs.

clue.text: Law of Swiss state banning introduction of tariffs

indicators.note: banning means shutting out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Switzerland is divided into states called cantons

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Legislation in a Swiss region outlawing the introduction of import duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or law, especially a church law.

clue.text: Learning of nude riot, I panicked

indicators.note: panicked letters scatter in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to panicking when caught up in a naked riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is scholarly knowledge, the fruit of much learning (noun).

clue.text: Tease short bloke very loudly

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: chap is British slang for a man, a bloke
FF is fortissimo in musical notation, very loud

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a small man at the top of their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like teasing a short man, but it docks CHAP to CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff is to banter with or rib someone, a light mockery.

clue.text: Iron resolution possessed by private secretary

indicators.note: being possessed by means being held within the other piece

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
res is short for resolution, as in high-res images

explanation.surface: An iron will held by a secretary, determined to the core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' tempts as the metal or firmness; it is the verb, to press clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing a garment with a hot iron smooths out its creases, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Order wine for relatives

parts.note: an order is a kind or class, as in biological ranks
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Someone orders wine for the family gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning sort: KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred is a collective term for one's family members, blood kin.
